description:
Sets NASA's pictures of the day as your wallpaper, on its own APODroid sets NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) as your wallpaper. A new picture comes out every day, and the app picks it up on its own. Turn on "More NASA pictures" to add NASA's Image of the Day and the Earth Observatory's Image of the Day. The app is one page: today's picture with its title and date, and the settings below it (beside it on tablets and in landscape). With more than one source, swipe or use the name above the picture to see each one. Pull down to refresh. Tap the picture to open it on NASA's website, or tap the star to save it to your gallery. Tap the frame button to choose which part of the picture becomes the wallpaper, or the whole picture on a blurred or black background; the check mark sets it. The astronomer's explanation starts under the title; tap it to read it all. Settings:
  • Change automatically: the wallpaper, on or off, at once.
  • Where (Setup, like the next two: a draft until you tap Set as wallpaper): home screen, lock screen, or both. With "More NASA pictures" on, Pictures from instead: each source on the home screen, the lock screen or both. Drag the sources into order. A screen with two or more takes turns in that order, every 24, 12, 6 or 3 hours. NASA and Earth Observatory post on weekdays only.
  • New picture at: the hour the wallpaper changes, 06:00 by default. A picture that comes out in the 3 hours after it still goes on, or turn on As soon as it's out to get each new picture within the hour.
  • Size: Centre, Auto (the frame on the picture's subject; a wide APOD goes on sideways unless NASA's text says it has an up) or Live: a wide picture moves across the home screen over the day (a live wallpaper, picked once in Android's picker).
  • Keep pictures sharp: enlarges a small picture at most 2×; the rest of the screen shows it blurred.
  • Centre when unsure: with Auto, a subject only slightly off the middle stays centred.
  • Darken bright pictures: on by default, so the clock and widgets stay readable.
  • If APOD is a video: skip it, use NASA's or Earth Observatory's picture, or a picture of your own. The page shows a ▶ tile (with a still from NASA's own videos) that opens the video on NASA's website.
  • Set as wallpaper: saves the setup and sets the wallpaper.
  • Advanced settings: save every new picture to your gallery, up to a size you choose; Keep running, so the phone can't stop the app between changes.
If Android would pause the app because you don't open it, a note below the picture names the settings that prevent it, for your phone's maker. If the phone stopped the app and a change came late, a note says so. Notes also tell you when the check fails. Privacy: no account, no ads, no tracking. The app talks only to NASA's websites (nasa.gov). Permissions: internet access, setting the wallpaper, network state, starting after a reboot (both for the daily update) and running as a foreground service (for Keep running, off by default). Saving to the gallery needs no permission. APODroid is not made by or affiliated with NASA.
